page.overview:
Who is Saint Lucia?

Saint Lucia was the youngest of the five companions of Alicia Dominica, the founder and patron saint of the Adepta Sororitas. Lucia went on to become the founder of the Order Majoris of the Sisters of Battle known as the Order of the Valorous Heart.

In the late 36th Millennium, Saint Lucia was captured by recidivists, who gouged out her eyes and forced her to endure the screams of a thousand innocents as they were tortured to death before her.

Unknown to Lucia, a group of her own sisters were amongst those put to death, but it is said that not one of them uttered a sound as they endured their tortures, so as not to cause Lucia any more pain than she had already suffered. Mere solar days after word of her death reached the Holy Synod, Lucia was canonised as an Imperial saint. Lucia is represented in Sororitas art by a woman with eyes shrouded and a drop of blood running down one cheek.

She may also carry a sword, held upright to symbolise her martial role within the Orders Militant. She may hold a skull in her left hand, which represents the severed head of High Lord Goge Vandire, which she is said to have recovered after Dominica put him to death, flensed, polished, carved with the Litanies and placed within the ancient archive of the Vault of Origins.
